acceptance: 1) Entry: admin Human conversations (admin-chat-link) -> /admin/chat -> actual row chat-thread-link-{id} -> /admin/chat/[id]. Data sources: GET /api/admin/chat/conversations and id GET/POST read. Clicking a real persisted conversation reads body/author. Only displayed messages are marked read; undisplayed new seq stays unread. Filtered/page snapshots are not treated as increment logs (E-31, E-34, E-79). 2) Reuse the 3s/hidden/backoff/single-in-flight component. Changing thread cancels old requests and late responses cannot overwrite. ADMIN/SALES may read. EDITOR sees no entry and direct API access returns 403. After a signed-in operator becomes EDITOR, next poll/send test requests have no body or write; UI clears the thread/stops timers. Visitor modifications of threadId/seq/email still grant no access (E-32, E-76, E-77, E-78). 3) Query failure is not a successful empty-items state. Show original actual failed/unknown/disabled notifications without changing message received. Do not promise operator online/read states (E-35, E-41). Use the unique minimalist-flat style from section 11. At the actual service at 1920x1080, 1440x900, and 390x844, record GIFs and computed styles: 2px black borders, zero radius, no shadow, and accent #b45700. On each admin page, run D1-D6 and overflow probes with work/form/card and density7/gutter16/gap16/pad16. Labels and keyboard focus are reachable; touch-control targets measure at least 44px.

E-31.scene: C-01 Human inbox and reply entry points
E-31.trigger: A visitor submits a message and server-side persistence succeeds.
E-31.expect: Return stable conversation and message identifiers and show Received, with the conversation readable in the operator inbox. If the database write fails, retain a retry-pending state and do not show Received or read by an operator.

E-32.scene: C-01 Human inbox and reply entry points
E-32.trigger: The requester is unauthenticated, an EDITOR, an account whose privileges were revoked, or a visitor guessing someone else's conversation identifier.
E-32.expect: Directly request the read and reply endpoints for each of these cases and verify no content is returned and no write occurs. Return data to ADMIN/SALES only under current authorization; hiding a button is not authorization evidence.

E-34.scene: C-01 Human inbox and reply entry points
E-34.trigger: A new message arrives while the inbox is refreshed or paginated.
E-34.expect: Apply the defined seq cursor and read MAX rules: insert messages between pages and verify that each message ID in the completed range appears exactly once. Advance read only to the seq actually confirmed by the user; newly arrived higher-seq messages remain unread.

E-35.scene: C-01 Human inbox and reply entry points
E-35.trigger: An email notification fails or is not connected.
E-35.expect: Represent the actual notification state using the defined queued/sending/sent/failed states or their existing DTO mapping. Notification failure after a message is saved changes only that notification state, not the message's received state or the inbox's ability to process it. An unconnected source must not display Sent.

E-41.scene: C-02 Offline messages and recovery from send failures
E-41.trigger: A message has been saved but an operator reply or notification fails to send.
E-41.expect: Keep the received result and inbox pending-work state. Separately show the real sending failure; do not pretend that the visitor has been contacted.

E-76.trigger: The chat/inbox is visible and requests succeed.
E-76.expect: Use a normal interval of three seconds. Pause while the tab is hidden; when visible again, immediately catch up from the confirmed seq. Slow networks or repeated failures use bounded backoff up to 30 seconds. No round may accumulate unbounded in-flight requests.

E-77.trigger: There are multiple tabs, retries, out-of-order responses, or new messages inserted between pages.
E-77.expect: Merge and deduplicate by stable server seq and message identifier. Advance the cursor only through the fully received range. A late old response must not move the cursor backward, overwrite a newer reply, or skip messages on an omitted page.

E-78.trigger: A visitor session expires or is revoked, or an operator loses chat permission after previously holding ADMIN/SALES.
E-78.expect: Perform server-side authorization on the next poll and send, and stop returning conversation content. Changing threadId, seq, or email cannot read another consultation.

E-79.trigger: The network recovers after an interruption, or the operator inbox has many unread messages.
E-79.expect: Bind bounded pages to the established pagination cap, verify that no request exceeds it, and continuously fill seq gaps. Polling updates only the confirmed-receipt cursor, not the user's read position, and must not create an operator-online or read promise.
